hero.headline: Energy is the New Oil, Compute is the New Gasoline
hero.subheadline: Traditional power projects suffer from low margins. We flip the script by using energy as a raw material for a global digital product.

sections.title: The Arbitrage Opportunity in Emerging Markets
sections.body: In many energy-rich developing nations, the power sector is hampered by a 'local demand ceiling.' You can generate gigawatts of electricity, but the local grid often lacks the industrial capacity to consume it at a profitable rate. Kenya AI Compute addresses this inefficiency through vertical integration. We don't sell electricity to the grid; we feed it directly into our GPU and CPU clusters. By doing so, we are performing a sophisticated form of energy arbitrage. We purchase or generate energy at an industrial cost of $0.04/kWh and export it via fiber optics as computational power, which is sold on the global market for $0.70-$1.00 per unit of GPU work. This effectively turns a local utility into a global high-tech exporter, shielded from local currency fluctuations and grid bottlenecks. sections.title: Why Arbitrage Works
items: Price Disparity: $0.04/kWh production cost vs. high-value global compute demand.
Zero Transmission Loss: Power is consumed within 200 meters of the generation source.
Currency Hedging: Costs are settled in local currency while revenue is strictly in USD.
Infinite Demand: The global AI market acts as a buyer of last resort for every watt we produce.
Regulatory Buffer: Operating in Special Economic Zones secures our low-cost base for decades.
